name: Train and certify field staff
summary: Field staff cannot go to a customer's location without current safety tickets such as the industry safety orientation, H2S Alive, standard first aid, WHMIS and dangerous goods, and they need service-line courses and supervisor sign-offs before they run equipment on their own. The HSE coordinator finds the need from the training matrix and the ticket expiry report, books seats in the company's training centre or with outside providers, and works with dispatch to free the worker from the rotation. The worker travels to the course, trainers deliver and assess the internal courses, certificates are entered in the learning management system, and for competency modules a field supervisor observes the task on location and signs it off. Seats, rotations and travel decide how fast a ticket is done, and hiring waves in 2021-2022 left new hires waiting for courses before they could work.

baseline.org_archetype: A listed Canadian pressure pumper of about 1,350 people, roughly 880 of them field staff on rotation or on call at nine district bases, with a Calgary head office for finance, HR, HSE and engineering.
baseline.notes: A training centre at the Red Deer base, outside providers for industry tickets, a learning management system that tracks expiry dates, spreadsheets of training matrices by position, and paper or PDF competency checklists signed in the field.

unit_of_work: one training enrolment (one worker completing one course or competency module)
trigger: A training need arrives: a new hire's missing tickets, a ticket expiring within 60 days on the expiry report, a crew scheduling request, a role change or an incident corrective action.
end_state: The worker's certificate or competency sign-off is recorded in the learning management system and visible to crew scheduling and on customer prequalification portals, or the enrolment is cancelled.

volume.seasonality: Heaviest in August to November before the winter season and in May to June during break-up, when crews are off the road and renewals are booked; light in January to March when crews are fully deployed.

evidence.note: About 880 field staff holding 4-6 tickets each on 3-year cycles gives roughly 100-150 renewals a month, plus 4-6 courses for each of about 30 new hires a month and service-line modules; agrees with the organisation file's 150-300-500.

surge.cause: Hiring wave for crew reactivation or pre-season staffing, with every new hire needing a full set of tickets

evidence.note: Adding field crews was difficult and the company competed to attract personnel (src4); multiplier estimated from four to six courses per new hire during a hiring drive.
Four coordinators; about half their time on training needs, bookings and record entry (about 25 minutes per enrolment).
Books outside course seats, pays course fees and arranges hotels for trainees from distant bases.
Eight instructors; about two thirds of their time delivering internal courses, the rest on course development, field coaching and audits.

Stands for all field trainees (pump, blender, cementing and coiled tubing operators and drivers): about 9-10 hours of course and travel time per enrolment at 300 enrolments a month. Role not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Observes and signs off service-line competencies on location. Role not listed for this process in the organisation file.

systems.name: Learning management and safety ticket tracking
HRIS, field time capture and payroll
Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)

resources.name: Crew pickup trucks and light vehicles

steps.name: Pick up training need
steps.description: The HSE coordinator receives the new hire list, crew scheduling requests, incident actions and the weekly LMS report of tickets expiring within 60 days, and opens a training request for each person and course.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check training matrix and existing certificates
steps.description: The coordinator looks up the position in the training matrix, checks the worker's LMS record and any certificate already held from a previous employer, and decides which course is needed and whether it runs in-house or with an outside provider.

error.defect_description: Wrong course or level chosen for the position

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Schedule into an internal class
steps.description: The coordinator adds the worker to the next internal class with a free seat (service-line orientation, pressure safety, equipment courses, WHMIS or driving), and waits when classes are full.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Release worker from rotation
steps.description: The coordinator asks the district dispatcher to keep the worker off the board for the class day and to arrange travel, and rebooks when the worker is called out to a job instead.

next.condition: called out to a job, rebook

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Book hotel and travel for distant trainees
steps.description: For workers from Grande Prairie, Fort St. John or other distant bases the HR coordinator books a hotel near the training centre, arranges a shared pickup and tells the worker where and when to report.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Travel to the training centre
steps.description: The worker drives from the home base or home to the training centre, often the evening before, in a company pickup with other trainees.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait out a winter storm
steps.description: When a blizzard or icy highways make the drive unsafe the worker stays at the base under the journey management rules, and the class is attended late or the seat goes to the next session.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Attend internal course
steps.description: The worker attends the classroom and hands-on parts of the course at the training centre, practises on equipment in the yard and writes the test.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act: employer ensures workers are properly trained and that hazardous work is done by competent workers

evidence.note: Employer duty to train and to use competent workers (src9); course lengths estimated at half a day to two days.

steps.name: Deliver and assess the class
steps.description: The trainer teaches the class of about ten to fifteen, runs the practical exercises, marks tests and records pass or fail; the minutes here are one trainee's share of the class plus marking.

next.condition: failed or did not finish, rebook

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Book a seat with an outside provider
steps.description: The HR coordinator books a seat with an authorised provider for H2S Alive, first aid, ground disturbance or dangerous goods courses, sends the worker's details and pays or commits the fee.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for the course date
steps.description: The outside course runs on its own calendar; in busy months the nearest seats are one to three weeks out and the worker must also be off rotation that day.

evidence.note: Provider sessions are scheduled classes with a fixed number of seats (20 for H2S Alive, src6); waits estimated.

steps.name: Travel to the outside course
steps.description: The worker drives in a company pickup to the provider's training site in Calgary, Nisku, Grande Prairie or another town, sometimes the evening before with an overnight hotel stay.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Attend outside course
steps.description: The worker completes the course and its practical tests, for example a one-day H2S Alive class with breathing apparatus drills or a two-day standard first aid course.

evidence.note: H2S Alive is one day with practical SCBA components and a 70% pass mark (src6); standard first aid is a two-day, 14-hour course (src8).

steps.name: Provider issues the certificate
steps.description: The provider records the result and issues the certificate or wallet card, by email the same week or through the industry training record.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Pay course fee and charge the cost centre
steps.description: When the certificate arrives the HR coordinator matches the provider invoice to the booking and attendance, codes it to the trainee's district and service line and sends it for payment.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Record certificate in the LMS
steps.description: The HSE coordinator checks the certificate's name, course and dates, scans it to the employee file and enters the completion and expiry date in the LMS.

control.basis: Customer and certifying-body audits of training records (COR audits and prequalification reviews)

evidence.note: Certificates carry three-year validity for H2S Alive and first aid (src6, src8), which the LMS expiry date tracks; time estimated.

steps.name: Wait for the task on location
steps.description: The worker returns to the crew; a competency such as running a pump from the control van or rigging up treating iron can only be observed when the crew does that task on a job.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Observe and sign off competency
steps.description: The field supervisor watches the worker do the task on location, asks the checklist questions, coaches on gaps and signs the checklist, or records that more practice is needed.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act: work that may endanger a worker is done by a competent worker or under direct supervision of one

evidence.note: Competent-worker duty (src9); sign-off times estimated.

steps.name: Record competency sign-off
steps.description: The HSE coordinator receives the signed checklist from the base, checks every item is initialled, files it, marks the competency complete in the LMS and refreshes the ticket report that dispatchers and the progression review use.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Update scheduling and prequalification records
steps.description: The coordinator refreshes the ticket report used by dispatchers and uploads training records to the customer prequalification portals that ask for them.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Worker called out to a job
exceptions.description: The worker is dispatched on the class day and the course is rebooked.

exceptions.name: Failed course
exceptions.description: The worker fails or does not finish and is rebooked into a later class.

exceptions.name: Competency not yet shown
exceptions.description: The supervisor records that more practice is needed and observes again on a later job.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from training need to record in the LMS
benchmarks.population: Field safety tickets and competency modules at a WCSB service company, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: one to three weeks to the next free seat and rotation gap for tickets; four to eight weeks for competencies that wait for the task on a job.

benchmarks.population: Canadian Red Cross Standard First Aid
Energy Safety Canada general orientation for new workers

evidence.note: Current Common Safety Orientation; the orientation courses used in 2019-2022 were of similar length.

pain_points.description: New hires cannot go to location until their tickets are done, and in hiring waves internal classes filled up weeks ahead.

evidence.note: Organisation file description of training overload in 2021-2022; waits estimated.

pain_points.description: Training competes with the rotation: workers are pulled for jobs and classes are rebooked.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Competency checklists travel on paper from the field and are filed weeks after the sign-off.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Expiry tracking depends on manual entry of certificates from many providers into the LMS and then the customer portals.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Trican Well Service Ltd. Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: Three Tier 4 DGB fleets (126,000 HHP) operating at end 2022; fourth fleet (42,000 HHP) field ready by end Q1 2023 and fifth approved for early 2024; upgrades include 3,000 HHP continuous duty pumps and idle reduction packages; fully electric sand, blending and chemical equipment developed; capital spending $103.6 million in 2022 mainly Tier 4 upgrades; supply chain challenges such as long lead times on key parts; record inflation; difficulty adding field crews and attracting and retaining qualified personnel; recruiting events; CEWS credited against personnel expenses in 2021 ($10.2 million in cost of sales); the company has safety and training programs; MD&A dated February 22, 2023.

sources.title: H2S Alive course
sources.supports: One-day classroom course with a three-year certificate; practical SCBA donning and rescue drag components; 70% exam pass mark; sessions of 20 seats.

sources.title: Common Safety Orientation (CSO)
sources.supports: One-day general safety orientation for workers new to the energy industry, online or classroom, certificate does not expire. Current successor of the orientation courses used in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Standard First Aid & CPR fact sheet
sources.supports: Two-day course, CPR C 14 hours in class or blended; 3-year certification; recertification 7.5 hours in class for CPR C.

sources.title: Obligations of work site parties
sources.publisher: Government of Alberta (Occupational Health and Safety)
sources.supports: Employers must ensure workers are properly trained, supervised by competent supervisors, and that work that may endanger a worker is done by a competent worker or under the direct supervision of one.

assumptions: Loaded costs are the organisation file's (base wage x 1.35).
The frac pump operator role stands for all field trainees; trainee time (travel and course) is most of the labour in this process.
Trainer minutes per enrolment are one trainee's share of a class of about ten to fifteen; the trainer step runs alongside the trainee's attendance and adds no elapsed time.
Field supervisors and the trainees take part although the process map lists only trainer, HSE coordinator and HR coordinator.
Crew scheduling requests (training_enrolment) and new hires from recruitment (training_need) are added as triggers; the process map has only onboarding and incidents.
About half of enrolments are internal courses and four in ten outside courses; one in ten finds a valid certificate already held.
